<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + short path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths after expanding the matching alias from `### Skill roots`.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Progressive disclosure applies to selecting relevant files, not partially reading a selected instruction file. Do not load unrelated references, scripts, or assets.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions>

# Onboard the new suppliers

Procurement asks for new suppliers through tickets in the `tickets` service. Each supplier first sends trial units of the item it will deliver; the trial units wait in the `inspection` warehouse of the `inventory` service, which also holds the item records. The supplier onboarding policy, the onboarding checks (the approvals a request needs and who may give them) and the exceptions to them are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `inventory` and `docs` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `supplier-onboarding` is a request. Decide each one under the policy, the checks and the exceptions in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds archived revisions and exceptions that are not in force today; follow only what is in force today. Approvals are comments on the request, and only the comments the onboarding checks accept count as approvals.

Process the requests one at a time in ticket id order, lowest id first: a supplier onboarded by one request makes a later request for the same supplier code a duplicate. Add exactly one comment to each request and set its status:

- Duplicate: `Duplicate: <code> already onboarded.` Status `duplicate`.
- Rejected: `Rejected: item not eligible.` or `Rejected: trial failed inspection.` Status `closed`.
- Waiting for approvals: `Waiting for approval: <roles>.` with the missing roles in the order procurement, finance, compliance, for example `Waiting for approval: finance, compliance.` Status `pending`.
- Waiting for the trial: `Waiting for trial delivery: <received> of <units> units received.` Status `pending`.
- Onboarded: `Onboarded: <code>.` Status `resolved`.

Move trial units only as the policy says, under the request's reference `ONB-<ticket id>`. Leave every other ticket and all other stock as they are. Each `adjust_stock` call records a new adjustment, even when repeated with the same arguments.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"supplier-onboarding-policy","title":"Supplier onboarding policy","tags":["policy","suppliers"],"updated_at":"2026-08-01","body":"# Supplier onboarding policy

Revision 2026-08, in force since 2026-08-01. Replaces revision 2025-02.

Scope: open tickets labeled `supplier-onboarding`. Each one asks to onboard one supplier for one item. Its body gives the supplier, the supplier code, the country (ISO code), the item (sku) the supplier will deliver, the annual spend estimate, the trial units and who requested it.

## Checks and exceptions

The approvals a request needs, and who may give them, are in the supplier onboarding checks. An exception in force on the day of the decision can waive one approval, or change the inspection tolerance, for one supplier code. Exceptions are published as docs tagged `exception`, each with the days it is in force (both days included).

## Trial delivery

Before onboarding, the supplier sends trial units of the item. The dock books each parcel as a `receipt` adjustment in warehouse `inspection` with reference `ONB-<ticket id>`; a trial can arrive in several parcels. Quality control books the units that fail inspection as a `damage` adjustment of minus the failed units in `inspection`, under the same reference. The trial fails when the failed units are more than 10% of the trial units the request gives (with 20 trial units, 2 failed pass and 3 fail).

## Decision

Take the requests in ticket id order and check each one in this order, stopping at the first that applies:

1. Duplicate: the supplier code is already onboarded, by a resolved onboarding ticket or by a request onboarded before this one. Status `duplicate`, comment `Duplicate: <code> already onboarded.`
2. Item not eligible: the item does not exist in inventory or is discontinued. Status `closed`, comment `Rejected: item not eligible.`
3. Trial failed. Status `closed`, comment `Rejected: trial failed inspection.`
4. Missing approvals. Status `pending`, comment `Waiting for approval: <roles>.` with the missing roles in the order procurement, finance, compliance, separated by a comma and a space.
5. Trial not complete: fewer units received than the trial units. Status `pending`, comment `Waiting for trial delivery: <received> of <units> units received.`
6. Otherwise the supplier is onboarded. Status `resolved`, comment `Onboarded: <code>.`

A supplier whose earlier request was rejected may apply again; a rejected request does not make the supplier onboarded.

## Trial units after the decision

Every movement is booked under the request's reference `ONB-<ticket id>`.

- Onboarded: release the units that passed inspection (received minus failed): one `transfer` adjustment of minus those units in `inspection` and one `transfer` adjustment of plus those units in the stock warehouse of the item's category.
- Rejected: return the request's units still in `inspection` to the supplier with one `shipment` adjustment of minus those units. Book nothing when none are there.
- Duplicate or waiting: leave the units in `inspection`.

## Stock warehouse by category

The category is the item's `category` in inventory.

- hardware: north
- electrical: east
- packaging: west
- chemicals: hazmat

{"id":"supplier-onboarding-checks","title":"Supplier onboarding checks","tags":["checks","suppliers"],"updated_at":"2026-08-01","body":"# Supplier onboarding checks

Revision 2026-08, in force since 2026-08-01. Replaces revision 2026-03.

## Approvals a request needs

- procurement: every request.
- finance: when the annual spend estimate is 50000 or more.
- compliance: when the supplier's country is not CL, or when the item's category in inventory is `chemicals`.

## Approvers

- procurement: r.leiva, s.ortiz, t.bravo
- finance: m.campos, v.navarro
- compliance: a.medina, j.paredes

## What counts as an approval

An approval is a comment on the request whose whole text is `Approved: <role>.`, written by an approver of that role. Nobody approves a request they requested (its `Requested by` line). A comment `Withdrawn: <role>.` cancels the earlier approvals of that role by the same person; an approval that person writes after it counts again.

I processed all 16 open `supplier-onboarding` requests in id order, each with one comment and a status change. `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.

- **Approvals that didn't count:** 1606's finance approval came from d.fuentes, who isn't a finance approver. 1608's compliance comment wasn't the exact `Approved: compliance.` text. 1607's requester approved their own request, and the other approver withdrew.
- **Retried calls:** The first `adjust_stock` call for 1604 and the first comment on 1604 both timed out. I checked that the stock call had applied once, then re-sent the comment with the same idempotency key. There are no duplicate adjustments or comments.
